sections.html:
Midvale is a small, tightly built city, with the Jordan River on one side and Interstate 15 through its middle. The 2020 count was 36,028 people, against 27,964 in 2010, and much of that growth was new housing on former smelter land to the west.

Just 43.4% of Midvale homes are lived in by their owners. So the person selling is often a landlord, an heir to a rental, or an owner with a tenant still inside. Owner-occupied homes have a median value of $436,600. Median gross rent is $1,597, households average 2.30 people, and density is 6,092 people per square mile. All of this describes the city broadly and says little about one particular house.

sections.h2: Bingham Junction and the old slag site
sections.html:
Bingham Junction is 446 acres on the west side where five smelters worked lead and copper ore from 1871 to 1958. The EPA lists the ground as the Midvale Slag Superfund site. A Ready for Reuse Determination in 2008 cleared it for commercial and residential use.

It now holds a light rail station that opened in 2011, a mix of housing types, offices, a supermarket and a park. Just south, Jordan Bluffs covers 351 acres of the same slag ground. Building there is still early, though proposals could bring around 3,500 homes.

Own a house on the west side? Lenders and buyers sometimes ask about the area's past. Dig out whatever closing or cleanup papers you got at purchase, and ask the title company about the specific parcel. Expect buyers near the station to weigh your house against newer townhomes and condos.

Two TRAX lines, Interstate 15 and a quick hop to Interstate 215 keep most valley commutes manageable. Average travel time to work is 20.6 minutes.

  • The Red Line serves Bingham Junction and continues to the University of Utah.
  • The Blue Line serves Midvale Fort Union and Midvale Center.
  • 7800 South is the main east-west street, and Main Street (700 West) runs through the historic downtown.
  • The I-15 and I-215 interchange is near 7200 South and State Street, where a ski bus also runs.

Shopping clusters at the Shops at Fort Union and along State Street. A house within walking distance of a station should say so in its listing.

Midvale's west side grew around rail and smelting, and the east side moved from farmland to housing. Nearly all of the housing is under a century old, with many homes built in recent decades.

The bigger concern is the ground. The Wasatch Fault runs along the valley, and experts put the odds of a magnitude 6.0 or larger quake somewhere on it within 50 years at 57 percent. Soft Lake Bonneville sediments under much of the Wasatch Front raise liquefaction risk. A magnitude 5.7 quake near Magna in March 2020 was felt across the valley.

An inspector going through an older Midvale house will likely flag chimneys, water heater strapping and foundation cracks. You can fix them, disclose them, or sell as-is and let the buyer decide.

Renting out a house in Midvale takes a landlord business license from city hall. Yours runs out on August 31 and the renewal deadline is September 15. Most other business licenses run out December 31 and are late after January 15.

The council sets fees each year, and a business that relocates within Midvale gets new inspections. If you rent the house you are selling, make sure the license is paid up before an agent asks. The business licensing office can answer questions about your account.

Salt Lake County values and bills every Midvale parcel on a single countywide timetable, using each property's condition and market on January 1.

Tax stepDate
Assessor certifies valuesMay 22
Valuation notices mailedJuly and August
Board of Equalization window45 days from the original mailing
Tax notices mailedBy November 1
Last day to pay without penaltyNovember 30
Taxes become delinquentDecember 1

Disagree with a valuation notice? The Board of Equalization window in the table is the time to contest it.

An owner-occupied home in Utah is assessed at 55 percent of market value because of a 45 percent residential exemption. A sale does not carry the break over. Whoever buys and moves in must apply, with filings due at the county Board of Equalization by September 15. Tell a buyer about it, since skipping the form means taxes on the full value.

sections.h2: Recording a deed with the county
sections.html:
Take a deed to the county recorder at 2001 South State Street, Suite N1-600. The counter is staffed Monday through Friday, 8 a.m. to 5 p.m. The office will not write a document for you, notarize it, or judge whether the title is clean.

Once a deed is processed and imaged, the original comes back by mail in two to three weeks. A title company normally files on your behalf, so a visit is rarely needed.

sections.h2: How a cash sale works in Midvale
sections.html:
Midvale deeds get recorded the usual way, yet a cash deal drops the lender, the appraiser and the back-and-forth over repairs. Here is the sequence.

  1. Tell us what the place is like: who lives there, what needs work, what paperwork is missing.
  2. We look it over and send a price.
  3. Say yes, and a title company sets up the signing and files the deed.
  4. Pick a closing day that suits you and the title company.

A rental with tenants, a house with deferred maintenance or one with inherited paperwork can go as-is. Saying no to our price costs you nothing. Ahead of that first conversation, collect the lease and rent roll, the newest tax notice and anything on the property's history.

A tenant in the house does not stop you from selling. Put the lease and rent roll in the buyer's hands early, so the closing day can work around when the lease ends. Landlords should confirm that the city license is up to date and the tax bill is paid. A balance left after December 1 is delinquent and is cleared out of the proceeds at closing.

sections.h2: Paperwork to gather before you sell
sections.html:
A little preparation keeps a Midvale sale moving. Look for your deed or closing statement, the latest valuation and tax notices, any landlord license renewal, tenant leases with the rent roll, and receipts for major repairs. If the house came to you through an estate, add whatever probate or transfer papers exist. Gaps are common and a title company can usually work around them, but knowing what you have lets you answer questions fast.

Look over the house itself too. Note the age of the roof, furnace and water heater, because a cash buyer prices those in instead of asking you to repair them first.

faqs.q: What is the population of Midvale, Utah?
faqs.a: It was 36,028 at the 2020 count, up 28.8 percent from 27,964 in 2010.

faqs.q: When are Midvale property taxes due?
faqs.a: The penalty-free deadline is November 30. A bill still open on December 1 is delinquent.

faqs.q: Do I need a license to rent out a house in Midvale?
faqs.a: Yes. The city issues a landlord business license, which runs out August 31 and must be renewed by September 15.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Midvale house that has tenants in it?
faqs.a: Yes, and many here do. Share the lease and rent roll with the buyer at the outset so the closing date matches the lease.
